  1. 1

    Which of these expressions names a real number, and what is its value: −324\sqrt[4]{-32}4−32​ or −325\sqrt[5]{-32}5−32​?

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Applies the odd-root sign convention to an even index, as if a fourth root could return a negative number.

    You chose C: Assumes that an even root failing to be real for a negative radicand means no root at any index can succeed, overlooking that the index 555 is odd.

    You chose D: Forgets that an even-indexed root of a negative radicand has no real value at all.

    For an odd index, every real number has exactly one real nnn-th root, and it carries the sign of the radicand: −325=−2\sqrt[5]{-32} = -25−32​=−2 because (−2)5=−32(-2)^5 = -32(−2)5=−32. For an even index, a negative radicand has no real root at all, so −324\sqrt[4]{-32}4−32​ is not a real number.

    −325=−2,−324 is not real\sqrt[5]{-32} = -2, \qquad \sqrt[4]{-32} \text{ is not real}5−32​=−2,4−32​ is not real

  2. 2

    Evaluate 32−3/532^{-3/5}32−3/5.

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Flips the sign of the value instead of taking a reciprocal.

    You chose C: Drops the negative exponent instead of reciprocating.

    You chose D: Reciprocates correctly but then also flips the sign of the result.

    A negative exponent means take the reciprocal, not flip the sign. Take the fifth root first, then cube it.

    32−3/5=1323/5=1(325)3=123=1832^{-3/5} = \frac{1}{32^{3/5}} = \frac{1}{\left(\sqrt[5]{32}\right)^3} = \frac{1}{2^3} = \frac1832−3/5=323/51​=(532​)31​=231​=81​

    Solve 6x+3=x−4\sqrt{6x + 3} = x - 46x+3​=x−4.

    Answer choices for question 4

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Filters candidates by whether the radicand is nonnegative rather than substituting into the original equation; both 6(1)+36(1)+36(1)+3 and 6(13)+36(13)+36(13)+3 are positive, so this check wrongly passes both.

    You chose B: Checks against the sign-flipped twin equation 6x+3=−(x−4)\sqrt{6x+3} = -(x-4)6x+3​=−(x−4) instead of the original.

    You chose C: Squares the equation as 6x+3=x2+166x+3 = x^2 + 166x+3=x2+16, dropping the cross term from (x−4)2(x-4)^2(x−4)2.

    Square both sides, solve the quadratic, then check each candidate in the original equation.

    6x+3=(x−4)2=x2−8x+16  ⟹  x2−14x+13=0  ⟹  (x−13)(x−1)=06x+3 = (x-4)^2 = x^2 - 8x + 16 \;\Longrightarrow\; x^2 - 14x + 13 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; (x-13)(x-1) = 06x+3=(x−4)2=x2−8x+16⟹x2−14x+13=0⟹(x−13)(x−1)=0

    At x=13x=13x=13: 81=9\sqrt{81}=981​=9 and 13−4=913-4=913−4=9, a match. At x=1x=1x=1: 9=3\sqrt9=39​=3 and 1−4=−31-4=-31−4=−3, which disagree, so x=1x=1x=1 is extraneous.

  20. 20

    For which values of xxx is (x+5+2−x)(x+5−2−x)\left(\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt{2-x}\right)\left(\sqrt{x+5}-\sqrt{2-x}\right)(x+5​+2−x​)(x+5​−2−x​) a real number, and what does it equal there?

    Answer choices for question 20

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Computes the conjugate-pair simplification correctly but ignores that each individual square root requires a nonnegative radicand.

    You chose C: Wrongly generalizes from the single boundary value x=2x=2x=2, where (x+5)−(2−x)=7(x+5)-(2-x)=7(x+5)−(2−x)=7, to the whole domain.

    You chose D: Enforces only the first radicand's condition, x+5≥0x+5\ge0x+5≥0, and forgets the second, 2−x≥02-x\ge02−x≥0.

    The product is a conjugate pair, so it simplifies to a difference of squares, but BOTH square roots must independently be real first.

    (x+5+2−x)(x+5−2−x)=(x+5)−(2−x)=2x+3\left(\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt{2-x}\right)\left(\sqrt{x+5}-\sqrt{2-x}\right) = (x+5)-(2-x) = 2x+3(x+5​+2−x​)(x+5​−2−x​)=(x+5)−(2−x)=2x+3

    Each radical needs a nonnegative radicand: x+5≥0x+5\ge0x+5≥0 and 2−x≥02-x\ge02−x≥0, which together give −5≤x≤2-5\le x\le2−5≤x≤2.

      Part B.

      A classmate instead squares both sides directly, writing (2x+6)−(x+1)=12(2x+6)-(x+1)=1^2(2x+6)−(x+1)=12, and concludes x=−4x=-4x=−4. Identify the specific algebra error, and explain why x=−4x=-4x=−4 could never have been a genuine solution regardless of the error.

      Find and correct the error Say which line first goes wrong, why it is wrong, and then do it correctly. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    no real solution (the quadratic x2+4x+12=0x^2+4x+12=0x2+4x+12=0 has a negative discriminant).

    Part B

    The student squared term by term, using (A−B)2=A2−B2(A-B)^2=A^2-B^2(A−B)2=A2−B2, which is false; squaring a difference must expand the cross term. Also x=−4x=-4x=−4 fails the domain, since x+1=−3<0x+1=-3<0x+1=−3<0 makes x+1\sqrt{x+1}x+1​ not even real.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Isolate one radical, square, isolate the surviving radical, and square again.

    2x+6=1+x+1  ⟹  x+4=2x+1  ⟹  (x+4)2=4(x+1)  ⟹  x2+4x+12=0\sqrt{2x+6}=1+\sqrt{x+1} \;\Longrightarrow\; x+4=2\sqrt{x+1} \;\Longrightarrow\; (x+4)^2=4(x+1) \;\Longrightarrow\; x^2+4x+12=02x+6​=1+x+1​⟹x+4=2x+1​⟹(x+4)2=4(x+1)⟹x2+4x+12=0

    The discriminant is 16−48=−3216-48=-3216−48=−32, which is negative, so there is no real candidate at all.

    Part B

    The classmate's step treats (2x+6−x+1)2(\sqrt{2x+6}-\sqrt{x+1})^2(2x+6​−x+1​)2 as (2x+6)−(x+1)(2x+6)-(x+1)(2x+6)−(x+1), which is the false rule (A−B)2=A2−B2(A-B)^2=A^2-B^2(A−B)2=A2−B2; the correct expansion keeps a cross term.

    (A−B)2=A2−2AB+B2≠A2−B2(A-B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2 \ne A^2 - B^2(A−B)2=A2−2AB+B2=A2−B2

    Independent of that error, x=−4x=-4x=−4 gives x+1=−3<0x+1=-3<0x+1=−3<0, so x+1\sqrt{x+1}x+1​ is not even a real number there, meaning x=−4x=-4x=−4 could never have satisfied the original equation.

    In one line

    2x+6−x+1=1\sqrt{2x+6}-\sqrt{x+1}=12x+6​−x+1​=1 has no real solution: isolating and squaring twice leads to x2+4x+12=0x^2+4x+12=0x2+4x+12=0, whose discriminant is negative. A classmate's shortcut of squaring term by term, (2x+6)−(x+1)=1(2x+6)-(x+1)=1(2x+6)−(x+1)=1, is not a legal expansion of (A−B)2(A-B)^2(A−B)2, and its candidate x=−4x=-4x=−4 also falls outside the domain.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

    1

    Recognizes that a negative discriminant means the equation has no real solution at all. . Worth 1 point.

    Part B 3 points

    2

    Names the term-by-term squaring error specifically, contrasting it with the correct expansion of (A−B)2(A-B)^2(A−B)2. . Worth 2 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    1

    Notes that x=−4x=-4x=−4 falls outside the domain independent of the squaring error. . Worth 1 point.

  8. 8

    8. A formula that stops being real before the algebra says so . 9 points. Question 8 of 10.

    9 pts

    A physics model gives the speed (in meters per second) of a wave on a string as v=45−5x2v = \sqrt{45 - 5x^2}v=45−5x2​, where xxx is a tension parameter.

    1. A
      Part A.

      For what values of xxx does v=45−5x2v=\sqrt{45-5x^2}v=45−5x2​ represent a real speed?

      Write the expression An equation or an expression is enough here. Show how you built it. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Evaluate vvv at x=1x=1x=1, in simplest radical form.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      Suppose someone evaluates vvv at x=4x=4x=4 without first checking the domain from part A. Explain what goes wrong, referencing the parity of the index.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    −3≤x≤3-3 \le x \le 3−3≤x≤3.

    Part B

    2102\sqrt{10}210​ m/s.

    Part C

    At x=4x=4x=4 the radicand is 45−5(16)=−3545-5(16)=-3545−5(16)=−35, which is negative. Since the index is even, a negative radicand names no real number, so vvv is undefined there, exactly why part A restricted xxx to [−3,3][-3,3][−3,3].

    Worked solution

    Part A

    An even-indexed root needs a nonnegative radicand.

    45−5x2≥0  ⟹  x2≤9  ⟹  −3≤x≤345-5x^2 \ge 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; x^2 \le 9 \;\Longrightarrow\; -3 \le x \le 345−5x2≥0⟹x2≤9⟹−3≤x≤3

    Part B

    Substitute and extract the perfect square factor from the radicand.

    v=45−5(1)2=40=4⋅10=210 m/sv = \sqrt{45-5(1)^2} = \sqrt{40} = \sqrt{4\cdot10} = 2\sqrt{10} \text{ m/s}v=45−5(1)2​=40​=4⋅10​=210​ m/s

    Part C

    Because vvv is defined by a square root, an even-indexed root, a negative radicand means the expression names no real number: vvv is simply undefined at x=4x=4x=4. This is exactly the boundary that part A's domain restriction, −3≤x≤3-3 \le x \le 3−3≤x≤3, was set up to exclude.

    45−5(4)2=45−80=−35<0⟹v=−35 is not real45 - 5(4)^2 = 45 - 80 = -35 < 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad v = \sqrt{-35} \text{ is not real}45−5(4)2=45−80=−35<0⟹v=−35​ is not real

    In one line

    The formula is real for −3≤x≤3-3\le x\le3−3≤x≤3; at x=1x=1x=1, v=40=210v=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10}v=40​=210​ m/s. At x=4x=4x=4 the radicand is 45−80=−35<045-80=-35<045−80=−35<0, so the even-indexed root gives no real number there, which is exactly the boundary part A found.

    Rubric

  9. 9

    9. Why a cube root needs more than a sign flip . 6 points. Question 9 of 10.

    6 pts

    A student wants to rationalize 173−2\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]7-2}37​−21​ and reaches for the ordinary conjugate, multiplying by 73+2\sqrt[3]7+237​+2.

    1. A
      Part A.

      Compute (73−2)(73+2)(\sqrt[3]7-2)(\sqrt[3]7+2)(37​−2)(37​+2), and state whether the denominator is now free of radicals.

      Write the expression An equation or an expression is enough here. Show how you built it. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Explain, in general terms using x=d3x=\sqrt[3]dx=3d​ for an irrational cube root (where ddd is rational but not a perfect cube) and aaa for a rational number, why a two-term sign flip can never fully clear such a cube root, while it always clears a square root.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    493−4\sqrt[3]{49}-4349​−4, which still contains a radical, so the denominator is not yet rational.

    Part B

    A square root's square, ddd, is rational, so (a+d)(a−d)=a2−d(a+\sqrt d)(a-\sqrt d)=a^2-d(a+d​)(a−d​)=a2−d needs only one cancellation. A cube root's square, x2=d23x^2=\sqrt[3]{d^2}x2=3d2​, is ALSO irrational, so (a+x)(a−x)=a2−x2(a+x)(a-x)=a^2-x^2(a+x)(a−x)=a2−x2 leaves that term behind; only x3x^3x3 is rational.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Expand as a difference of squares.

    (73−2)(73+2)=(73)2−4=493−4(\sqrt[3]7-2)(\sqrt[3]7+2) = (\sqrt[3]7)^2 - 4 = \sqrt[3]{49} - 4(37​−2)(37​+2)=(37​)2−4=349​−4

    Since 494949 is not a perfect cube, 493\sqrt[3]{49}349​ is irrational, so the denominator is still not rational.

    Part B

    For a square root d\sqrt dd​, the relation (d)2=d(\sqrt d)^2=d(d​)2=d is rational, so one sign flip already clears it. For a cube root x=d3x=\sqrt[3]dx=3d​, the square x2=d23x^2=\sqrt[3]{d^2}x2=3d2​ is ALSO irrational (only x3=dx^3=dx3=d is rational), so a sign flip leaves that term behind.

    (a+d)(a−d)=a2−d (rational),(a+x)(a−x)=a2−x2 (still irrational)(a+\sqrt d)(a-\sqrt d) = a^2 - d \ \text{(rational)}, \qquad (a+x)(a-x) = a^2 - x^2 \ \text{(still irrational)}(a+d​)(a−d​)=a2−d (rational),(a+x)(a−x)=a2−x2 (still irrational)

    A sign flip only ever cancels an ODD power of the new object; a cube root has two irrational powers standing in the way, not one.

    In one line

    (73−2)(73+2)=493−4(\sqrt[3]7-2)(\sqrt[3]7+2)=\sqrt[3]{49}-4(37​−2)(37​+2)=349​−4, still irrational, so the ordinary conjugate fails. In general, a square root's square is rational, but a cube root's square is still irrational, so a two-term sign flip leaves that squared term behind; only the cube itself is rational, which is why a three-term multiplier is needed.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

    1

    Determines whether a radical remains and states whether the resulting denominator is rational. . Worth 1 point.

    Part B 3 points

    2

    Identifies that an irrational cube root's square is also irrational, unlike a square root's square. . Worth 2 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    1

    States the general pattern clearly in terms of aaa and xxx. . Worth 1 point.

    10. Welding two pipe lengths, and the rule that would have gone wrong . 9 points. Question 10 of 10.

    9 pts

    A fabricator is joining two lengths of pipe cut from the same stock: side lengths 18\sqrt{18}18​ and 8\sqrt88​ meters for one frame, and widths 50\sqrt{50}50​ and 98\sqrt{98}98​ meters for another.

    1. A
      Part A.

      The frame's area is the product of its two side lengths, 18⋅8\sqrt{18}\cdot\sqrt818​⋅8​. Evaluate it.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      The two widths, 50\sqrt{50}50​ and 98\sqrt{98}98​ meters, need to be welded end to end. Find the total length in simplest form.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      Part A's product rule needs a≥0a\ge0a≥0 and b≥0b\ge0b≥0 to guarantee it lands on the correct nonnegative root. Explain why −18⋅−8\sqrt{-18}\cdot\sqrt{-8}−18​⋅−8​ could NOT be evaluated by the same product-rule step used in part A, and state what it equals instead.

      Carry your own answer forward Compare your complex-number result with whatever value you found in part A; use your part A result consistently in the comparison.

      Compare the two methods Say what each one costs you, and when you would reach for it. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    121212 m2^22.

    Part B

    12212\sqrt2122​ meters.

    Part C

    Both radicands are negative, so the product rule's hypothesis fails. Converting to iii-form first, (i18)(i8)=i2144=−12(i\sqrt{18})(i\sqrt8)=i^2\sqrt{144}=-12(i18​)(i8​)=i2144​=−12 (m2^22 in the analogous units), the NEGATIVE of part A's value, not 121212.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Both radicands are nonnegative, so the product rule applies directly.

    18⋅8=144=12 m2\sqrt{18}\cdot\sqrt8 = \sqrt{144} = 12 \text{ m}^218​⋅8​=144​=12 m2

    Part B

    Simplify each radical to expose a shared unit, then add the like radicals.

    50+98=52+72=122 meters\sqrt{50}+\sqrt{98} = 5\sqrt2 + 7\sqrt2 = 12\sqrt2 \text{ meters}50​+98​=52​+72​=122​ meters

    Part C

    The product rule ab=ab\sqrt a\sqrt b=\sqrt{ab}a​b​=ab​ requires a≥0a\ge0a≥0 and b≥0b\ge0b≥0; here both radicands are negative, so the hypothesis fails and the rule cannot be applied directly. Converting each factor to iii-form first,

    −18⋅−8=(i18)(i8)=i2144=−12,\sqrt{-18}\cdot\sqrt{-8} = (i\sqrt{18})(i\sqrt8) = i^2\sqrt{144} = -12,−18​⋅−8​=(i18​)(i8​)=i2144​=−12,

    which is the negative of part A's answer, not the 121212 that blindly applying the product rule to (−18)(−8)=144\sqrt{(-18)(-8)}=\sqrt{144}(−18)(−8)​=144​ would give.

    In one line

    18⋅8=12\sqrt{18}\cdot\sqrt8=1218​⋅8​=12 m2^22 and 50+98=122\sqrt{50}+\sqrt{98}=12\sqrt250​+98​=122​ meters. But −18⋅−8\sqrt{-18}\cdot\sqrt{-8}−18​⋅−8​ cannot use the same product-rule step, since both radicands are negative; converting to iii-form first gives (i18)(i8)=−12(i\sqrt{18})(i\sqrt8)=-12(i18​)(i8​)=−12, the negative of part A's answer.
